learningObjective: Count pipeline fill and drain slots in a three-stage, four-micro-batch schedule and connect the visible idle cells to the simple pipeline bubble formula.
mediumRationale: A deterministic space-time SVG is the smallest medium that aligns stage, time, and micro-batch identity while making occupied and idle slots countable. A three-by-six grid gives a concrete instance of the article's bubble equation without requiring animation or a full forward-backward schedule comparison.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout can show micro-batch dependencies but cannot preserve a regular time grid whose active and idle slots can be counted.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: deterministic cells align three stages over six time slots, preserve the diagonal dependency wave, and expose the exact utilization arithmetic.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: an HTML table could represent the schedule, but the established SVG timeline primitives provide clearer arrows, a continuous fill/drain boundary, and reliable print geometry.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: changing stage or micro-batch counts would add controls and state when one worked example is enough to derive the invariant.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the primary papers contain denser schedule figures and their public availability is not assumed to grant adaptation rights. No paper or deck figure, data, or layout is reused.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the ASCII timelines name a bubble but do not make the numerator and denominator in the bubble fraction spatially countable.

pages.insight: The preceding system-design slide discusses data collection, storage, preprocessing, privacy, and bias, but contains no distributed execution schedule.

The modeling slide gives the deck's only relevant distributed-training statement: data parallel workers copy the model, while model parallelism evaluates different model components on different machines. It does not mention stages, micro-batches, schedules, or bubbles.
The following production-serving slide moves to gating, monitoring, updates, and inference constraints, confirming that the local model-parallel discussion has no pipeline continuation.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page deck was text-indexed for pipeline parallelism, pipeline bubble, micro-batch, GPipe, PipeDream, 1F1B, interleaving, model parallelism, tensor parallelism, and distributed training. There are no pipeline-specific hits. Page 164 is the only conceptual model-parallel hit, so pages 163-165 were read as its full neighborhood. The deck supplies only a broad model-parallel distinction and no reusable schedule.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest mental model is why a pipeline with work available still has idle devices: dependencies force a diagonal wave, leaving P minus 1 empty slots during both fill and drain. The visual isolates the forward-wave utilization model used by the stated formula. With P = 3 and M = 4, useful stage-slots are PM = 12, elapsed stage-slots are P(M + P - 1) = 18, and 6 are idle, so the idle fraction is 6/18 = 1/3 = (P - 1)/(M + P - 1).

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages, reviewed pages 163-165 around the only model-parallel reference, and checked GPipe, PipeDream, Megatron-LM, official PyTorch pipeline documentation, and arXiv licensing guidance before selecting an original countable schedule.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description. Every active cell names its micro-batch, every idle cell contains a dot, stage and time axes are explicit, and solid dependency arrows plus fill and drain labels preserve meaning without color. The established visual-wide scroll container keeps 11-pixel SVG labels at full size on a 390 CSS-pixel viewport, shared theme tokens support dark mode, and print rules remove the minimum width while forcing a light high-contrast palette.
